Validate Training-Only Model Selection Within CV Folds

Source: R/cv_comparison.R
select_cv.Rd

Score a model-selection rule rather than a single model. In each fold the rule picks the candidate with the lowest training AIC, AICc, or BIC, and the result keeps the held-out predictions that candidate already made. No models are refitted.

Usage

select_cv(
  mod_list,
  criterion = c("AICc", "AIC", "BIC"),
  ties = c("error", "first"),
  keep_fits = FALSE
)

Arguments

mod_list

Named list of complete cross-validation results, all scored on the same folds and observations. Each must keep its training records (keep_selection = TRUE) or full fits (keep_fits = TRUE). Results from cross_validate_field() and cross_validate_mixed() always keep their records.

criterion

Training criterion, declared in advance: "AICc" (default), "AIC", or "BIC". It is computed from each candidate's training log-likelihood and parameter count K with the same rules as aic_tab() and bic_tab(). AICc needs more training observations than K + 1.

ties

What to do when two candidates have exactly the same training criterion. The default "error" marks the fold as failed. "first" picks the tied candidate listed first in mod_list. No tolerance is applied, so only exact ties count.

keep_fits

Logical. The default FALSE returns compact output. TRUE also returns the selected training fit of each fold in fits. This requires every candidate to have been run with keep_fits = TRUE, because records cannot rebuild a fit.

Value

A cross-validation result of the same class as the candidates that scores the selection procedure. Each fold's predictions, training values, and diagnostics come from the candidate chosen in that fold, and settings$backend is "training_selection". The result adds selection, which holds chosen (the candidate picked in each fold, NA where selection failed), tables (each fold's training table, with every candidate's K, log-likelihood, and criterion), and the criterion, ties, and candidates. Results from cross_validate(), cross_validate_glm(), and cross_validate_clogit() also record the metrics scored and metrics_dropped, and each candidate's candidate_settings. See multiScaleR_cv for the other elements.

How the procedure is scored

Suppose your plan is to fit several candidate models and keep the one with the lowest AICc. Scoring only the winner on held-out data would flatter it, because it was chosen after seeing all of the data. select_cv() scores the whole plan instead. In each fold it computes the training criterion of every candidate from its fit to that fold's analysis rows, picks the lowest, and keeps the held-out predictions that candidate made. Assessment outcomes and CV scores never choose the winner. The pooled score therefore evaluates the declared candidate set and rule. If you then tune the candidate set or the rule using these results, evaluate the final choice with an independent test set or an outer validation layer.

What the candidates must keep

Run every candidate with keep_selection = TRUE (compact records) or keep_fits = TRUE (full fits). A record holds the native training log-likelihood, the native and ecological parameter counts, the rows that entered the likelihood, their responses, trials, and frequency weights, the formula as text, the controls, and the original diagnostics. NB2 and Gamma records also hold the estimated or fixed nuisance parameter. A record holds no fitted model, design matrix, raster, or formula environment, so it is much smaller than a fit, although its row metadata still grows with the number of observations and folds. Keeping records adds no fitting and does not change which folds pass their diagnostics.

Before selecting, the function checks each record or fit against the fold's analysis rows and the recorded responses and weights. If a candidate keeps both records and fits, they must agree exactly. A record that could not be built makes selection fail in that fold, without changing the candidate's own result. Results that kept fits work without records. A result that kept neither must be run again with keep_selection = TRUE.

Which candidates can be combined

The candidates must pass the same checks as in cv_tab(), with identical folds and observations and comparable likelihoods. NB2 and Poisson candidates can share a count target. Gamma and Gaussian candidates can share a continuous target, scored with RMSE or MAE. An information criterion cannot compare a count likelihood with a continuous density. Conditional-choice candidates must also share their partial-likelihood method.

For results from cross_validate(), cross_validate_glm(), and cross_validate_clogit(), the procedure is scored on the metrics that every candidate recorded. A default Poisson candidate records "deviance" and a default NB2 candidate does not, so their selection keeps "rmse", "mae", and "neg_log_score". selection$metrics lists the metrics kept and selection$metrics_dropped those left out. Field and mixed-model candidates must record the same metrics. Bayesian results have no training likelihood and are rejected.

Penalties follow the native parameter counts, and scales and shapes estimated by multiScale_optim() count toward K.

  • Conditional choice: the sample size in AICc and BIC is the number of choice sets (one event each), not the number of alternatives.

  • Spatial fields: the coefficients, field SD, estimated range, and any observation dispersion count toward K. The integrated field values add nothing. The held-out joint block score is that of the model chosen in the fold.

  • Mixed models: the sample size is the number of analysis observations. The covariance parameters count toward K, and the integrated group effects add nothing.

Read the result

Read complete and selection$chosen first. A fold fails, and the pooled scores become NA, when a criterion cannot be computed, is not finite, or ties under ties = "error". selection$tables shows the training table behind each choice. For GLM and conditional-choice results, the shared settings are copied from the first candidate, named in settings$controls_from, and selection$candidate_settings holds every candidate's controls. NB2 and Gamma selections also keep the settings (settings$fold_settings) and distribution of the model chosen in each fold, including when a Poisson or Gaussian reference wins. GLM, conditional-choice, and mixed-model selections also keep every candidate's warnings and diagnostics in selection, and grouped-map labels (raster_groups) are kept for the chosen model. The score does not integrate parameter or selection uncertainty, add intervals, or establish calibration.

See also

cv_tab(), cross_validate(), cross_validate_glm(), multiScaleR_cv, aic_tab(), bic_tab(), and vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR").

Examples

data("landscape_counts")
data("surv_pts")
# Three spatial folds. The simulated coordinates are in meters.
folds <- spatial_cv_folds(crds(vect(surv_pts)), block_size = 1000, k = 3,
                          crs = 32617)

# keep_selection = TRUE stores the training likelihoods that select_cv() reads
candidates <- list(
  null = cross_validate_glm(counts ~ 1, landscape_counts, folds,
                            family = "poisson", keep_selection = TRUE),
  site = cross_validate_glm(counts ~ site, landscape_counts, folds,
                            family = "poisson", keep_selection = TRUE))
selected <- select_cv(candidates, criterion = "AICc")
selected$selection$chosen         # model picked by training AICc in each fold
#>  fold1  fold2  fold3 
#> "site" "site" "null" 
selected$selection$tables$fold1   # the training table behind the first pick
#> 
#> Model selection based on AICc:
#> 
#>      K   AICc Delta_AICc AICcWt Cum.Wt      LL
#> site 2 287.62       0.00   0.53   0.53 -141.72
#> null 1 287.86       0.24   0.47   1.00 -142.90
#> 
selected$summary                  # held-out scores of the whole procedure
#>          metric estimate        unit n_assessment n_scored weight_sum complete
#> 1          rmse 2.236579 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
#> 2           mae 1.668719 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
#> 3 neg_log_score 2.174640 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
#> 4      deviance 2.382543 observation          100      100        100     TRUE
